reasons.detail: R1 — `plugin update` without an id now builds `planInstalledPluginUpdates()` and prints plan results before `plan.apply()`, and enabled-package count validation is preserved in the shared helper.
R2 — A prompt is shown for bulk mode and the plan is applied only when input trimmed/lowercased equals `y`/`yes`; other inputs skip `plan.apply()`.
R3 — When bulk confirmation is declined (empty, `n/no`, or other text), code returns before `plan.apply()`, so package commits and installed files are unchanged.
R4 — `plugin update <name>` now resolves a single named package via `updateInstalledPlugin` and directly applies that entry; no bulk prompt is shown.

R5 — Bulk behavior now uses enabled-package filtering, preserves update result shape and reporting hooks, and keeps no-upgrade/no-updates logic via `upgradeForUpdateResults` mirroring prior update-all behavior.
R7 — When no enabled package has an update, it returns early with `upgradeSkip('no package updates')` and never calls the bulk confirmation prompt.

R6 — `src/lib/command-registry.js` now advertises `plugin update [name]` instead of `plugin update-all`, and `src/plugin.js` only handles `command === "update"` (no compatibility `update-all` path). Added/updated e2e tests verify help no longer includes `update-all` and that invoking `plugin update-all` fails with `unknown plugin command: update-all` while leaving package commit unchanged.
